evaluations.label: A
errors: States 'Target group 15-35 years' as a settled outcome; the transcript shows the target group was left open (15-35, under 65, 20-55, income-based all floated, then the group concluded objectives matter more than an age group).

Action item 'Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery' is not an assigned action; the UI designer only said to investigate whether a battery is needed at all, and the cradle was an offhand idea.
Lists the 'updated market research data' item as unassigned, although the marketing expert said she would email more age numbers herself.

Credits the 'market as standalone remote' under target market and bundles teletext, TV-only and colours as one list; also lists the find-it feature as a firm function without noting it was only agreed in principle.
strengths: Concise and scannable, covers the main research figures (75%, 80%, 10% of buttons).
Correctly records teletext dropped, voice recognition rejected on price and the 12.5 euro production limit.
Includes the rechargeable cradle and the infrared reasoning.
weaknesses: Misstates the target-group outcome as decided.
Action items are thin and partly invented; omits the project manager's minutes and slides, the questionnaire and summary, the individual role assignments and the missing-presentation issue.
Very terse bullets with little context; a reader who missed the meeting would not know who presented or why decisions were made.
Timestamps are loose and no speakers are identified.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Next step says the 'Working design presentation' was not yet on the server; in the transcript the industrial designer's working design was in the shared folder and it was the project manager's own presentation that was missing.
'channel-zapping ~65% of use time' misstates the figure; the marketing expert said people zap about 65% during an hour of use.

'Age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting' is a slight distortion; the discussion pointed to income or spending ability and to objectives (fashion, simplicity), not lifestyle or attitude.
'Submit before individual work session' for the questionnaire is a slight embellishment; it was to be completed after the meeting, before the lunch break.
strengths: Most complete coverage of research numbers, design direction, technical chain, price (25 euro retail, 12.50 production) and scope (TV only, no teletext).
Clear list of agreed functions including the lost-remote locator, hidden secondary functions, battery or cradle and fashionable look.
Captures post-meeting tasks: questionnaire and summary, individual workstreams (components, user interface, market trend watching), coach emails, and the marketing expert's promise to email age data.
Correctly says voice recognition was ruled out and that the target group was not narrowed by age.
weaknesses: Does not name owners for most next steps; the project manager's duty to post minutes and slides is not clearly stated.
Mislabels which presentation was missing from the server.
Does not clearly say the target group stayed unresolved; presents 'roughly under 65' as the target.

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition'; only teletext was a management decision, while voice recognition was dropped by the team on price and need.

'Unresolved Questions: Would adding a find my remote beep function fit within budget?' and 'Is it feasible to include advanced features without exceeding the production cost limit?' were never raised in this form; the group agreed on the locator function without a budget debate.

Attributes the LCD screen idea and sliding hatches to the user interface presentation; the LCD idea came from the marketing expert's research summary, and the sliding hatch came up in group discussion.
Says the group weighed younger users interested in voice recognition against a broader range as the main framing; it also omits that the group concluded not to define the target by age.
strengths: Two views (summary and outline) give a good chronological walk-through of the agenda, research findings, technical presentation and working design.
Correctly records the 12.50 euro production cost and 25 euro retail price, teletext removal, TV-only scope and the corporate colours and slogan.
Mentions the cradle idea and the large buttons, hidden secondary functions and locator.
weaknesses: States 'Action Items: (none)' despite clear next steps (minutes and slides, questionnaire and summary, individual work areas, marketing expert emailing age data).
Uses anonymous 'Speaker N' labels with no roles, which makes it harder to follow who owns what.
Invents 'unresolved questions' and misattributes the voice recognition decision.
Does not clearly state what was left open on the target group.

evaluations.label: D
errors: Several timestamps are off (for example the 25 euro price and colours cited at 24:50, the individual work items at 34:48 when they came near 35:00 to 35:56).

The 12.50 euro production ceiling is placed in the target-market bullet as weighing against voice recognition; this is fine, but 'the group did not settle' on a target market is the only place the open question is flagged, and the marketing expert's follow-up to email age numbers is left out.
strengths: Accurately states the target group stayed unsettled and lists the range of age ideas plus the income-based alternative.
Correctly captures the sliding panel idea, the project manager's caution about chip transmission, and the cost reasoning against voice recognition.
Records the file-sharing confusion correctly: the industrial designer's file is in the shared folder and the project manager's own presentation is not on the server.
Action items name the owner (project manager) for minutes and slides and for resolving the missing presentation; also covers questionnaire, summary, individual work areas and coach emails.
Well structured with a short summary up front, section headings and timestamps that make it easy to check against the recording.
weaknesses: Omits the marketing expert's commitment to email more age data before the next meeting.
Lists the project manager as 'Speaker 1' and uses generic labels for other speakers instead of roles.
Slightly wordy and vague in places ('Each area had a corresponding concept or work focus') without naming the components, interface and market-trend concepts.
Does not give the infrared rationale (no line of sight needed).

rationale: D is the most reliable: it keeps the target group correctly open, gets the decisions (no teletext, TV only, brand colours, voice recognition costly, hidden secondary functions, locator, cradle) right, and records owner-assigned actions and the real file-sharing issue. B is nearly as complete with strong detail on research, technical design and next steps, but it misidentifies which presentation was missing from the server, slightly distorts a few figures and framings, and gives no owners. C reads well as an outline but invents unresolved questions, credits voice recognition to management, and reports no action items at all. A is the shortest and weakest: it presents a 15-35 target group as settled, offers a partly invented action list, and omits most next steps.
